text:
marta: heads-up — recent perf run shows increased KV cache fragmentation and a few OOM spikes at the 95th percentile for long-chat workloads. want to discuss a "capacity painting" approach + GC policy to reduce tail failures. :thinking:

sam: can you drop the run link / flamegraphs? I'll run pprof and look for big temporary allocations.

marta: https://perf.internal/runs/2024/kv-frag-398 — attached heap snapshots and allocator traces. main symptom: steady growth in free-but-fragmented bytes and occasional alloc failures during sustained decodes.

raj: quick read: allocator is using fixed slabs (1MB, 4MB) and we get 4MB holes when many small entries are evicted. also see a pattern where workspace buffers are reserved per-request then thrown away instead of reused across decode+population. my initial thought: allow cross-phase buffer reuse and add a small compaction path.

leo: another angle — per-request soft cap. right now we reserve an optimistic max for each request, which piles up. instead cap reservation to something like: min(global_remaining / pending_requests, token_count * avg_kv_entry). avoids huge reservations for long-context but sparse actual kv usage.

anya: FYI, I noticed this started after the kernel selector bump last week — the new matmul tiling allocates bigger temporaries at some sequence lengths. could be indirectly increasing peak working set. we should confirm whether kernel selection changed workspace footprints.

infra-bot: CI: kv-allocator-sim #412 finished — 12/14 scenarios passed, 2 flaky (seed-dependent). logs: https://ci.internal/job/kv-allocator-sim/412 (artifact: allocator-trace.jsonl).

sam: ran an eviction sim comparing two policies: "coalesce-on-evict" (merge adjacent free segments) vs "per-bucket-lru" (fast, no coalesce). results: fragmentation_ratio down ~22% with coalesce, but evict_latency_p95 increased by ~3ms under 90% load. memory headroom increased and OOMs disappeared in that sim.

marta: 3ms tail for eviction seems acceptable if it prevents OOMs and reduces retry storms. can we hide that latency with async/background compaction triggered when load < 60%?

raj: yes — design idea: immediate eviction keeps latency low, but mark freed segments for background coalesce. compactor runs when global_utilization < compaction_threshold and merges adjacent free ranges incrementally. also add an adaptive soft-reserve multiplier: 0.6 under high load, 1.0 under low load.

leo: decode-stage holding is important — decoder often pins small kv pages per-token. if we expose a TTL for pinned prefixes (e.g., 30s of inactivity), we can expire stale pins and reclaim earlier. also consider reclaim-on-low-memory hook that can evict pinned but cold prefixes.

anya: to avoid regressions from kernel changes, propose we add a metric 'workspace_footprint_by_kernel' and add it to the perf regression check. current failure looks correlated: kernel_selector v2 chose a tiling with 2x temp buffer.

marta: rollout plan proposal:
  1) introduce per-request soft-cap config (canary first)
  2) enable background coalescing flag behind runtime toggle
  3) add compactor job that runs under low util windows
  4) add workspace_footprint_by_kernel to perf checks and hold kernel selector change if footprint increases significantly

sam: i'll own the simulation harness updates and add fragmentation_ratio + evict_latency_p95 metrics to the dashboard. will add a synthetic that mimics long-chat skew.

raj: i'll prototype the compactor + partial-free support in allocator. aim to have an internal experiment in ~2 working days. also want to try shrinking the smallest slab size to 512KB for small-key workloads.

marta: great. syncing tomorrow 10:00am to lock config values and canary plan. tagging infra and runtime leads for visibility. :thumbsup:

leo: one more note — batching heuristics: prefer batch_by_estimated_workspace_size rather than raw token count. small batches with big workspace items are the worst for fragmentation. let's add that to the checklist.

anya: also adding a short eval that runs long-chat traces with varying kernel selectors, allocator toggles, and eviction policies so we can diff memory profiles automatically.

marta: thanks all — will open RFC and rollout checklist after the sync.
